definition: The set of problems that arise when analyzing or modeling data in high-dimensional spaces, where data becomes increasingly sparse and distances become less meaningful.
details: The curse of dimensionality motivates techniques like dimensionality reduction and regularization, and helps explain why naive distance-based methods can struggle as the number of input features grows very large.
story: Think of a historian sorting through boxes of letters, building a picture of an era one sentence at a time. Think of it this way: The set of problems that arise when analyzing or modeling data in high-dimensional spaces, where data becomes increasingly sparse and distances become less meaningful. And here is the clever part: The curse of dimensionality motivates techniques like dimensionality reduction and regularization, and helps explain why naive distance-based methods can struggle as the number of input features grows very large. The words a model reads become the world it believes in. And that is Curse of Dimensionality — the unglamorous work everything else stands on.
